questions.question: What is the main practical advantage of Markdown files as agent memory over a vector database?
options: People and models can read, edit, diff and review them directly
questions.explanation: That is why CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and progress files are so widely used.

questions.question: Why does resolve() call Path.resolve() and then compare with the root, instead of checking the string for '..'?
options: Resolving follows symlinks and normalises the path, so links pointing outside and odd spellings are caught too
questions.explanation: A symlink inside the root can point anywhere; only the resolved path tells you where a write really goes.

questions.question: Why must the text in str_replace appear exactly once?
options: It forces the model to quote enough context, and makes an edit to an ambiguous place fail loudly instead of changing the wrong line
questions.explanation: In the demo, replacing '- ' failed with 'found 4 times', and nothing was changed.

questions.question: What is MEMORY.md for?
options: Storing every fact in one place
A short index, loaded into every system prompt, telling a new session what each memory file holds
questions.explanation: Progressive disclosure: the index is always visible, the files are read when needed.

questions.question: A memory tool raises an exception on a bad path, and the agent loop crashes. What is the fix?
options: Return the error as a string observation, so the model can see it and try something else
Ask the user to fix the path
questions.explanation: Errors are observations (Phase 2 · Lesson 5). The loop carries on, and the bad write never happens.

questions.question: How did session 2 know what to do next, with no shared conversation?
options: It read progress.md, which session 1 wrote before stopping, after the index pointed to it
questions.explanation: Write progress before stopping, read it when starting: the hand-off between context windows.
